stream notes / expected+observed reference-frame coverage:
  -auto-alt-ref 1 -lag-in-frames 16 -g 250 -keyint_min 250 -cpu-used 0 -frame-parallel 0,
  2-pass. -frame-parallel 0 is REQUIRED and was added after discovering (self-review,
  not part of the original recipe) that ffmpeg's default frame-parallel='auto' resolved
  to frame_parallel_decoding_mode=1 on every frame of an earlier version of this stream
  -- per spec refresh_probs() (6.1.2), backward probability adaptation
  (adapt_coef_probs()/adapt_noncoef_probs()) only runs when
  error_resilient_mode==0 AND frame_parallel_decoding_mode==0; with fpdm=1 this
  stream would have silently carried ZERO backward adaptation despite being this
  wave's designated adaptation fixture ('the adaptation workhorse... so backward
  probability adaptation bugs surface'). Confirmed fixed: fpdm=0 on all 13 coded
  frames of the shipped stream (see the fpdm/refresh_ctx/ctx_idx/reset_ctx columns
  in the per-frame table below, and 'adapt=YES' on every frame).
  1-pass vs 2-pass and lag-in-frames bisection (properly isolated -- lag alone,
  independent of the pass-count switch): lag=8 in 2-pass genuinely produces ZERO
  hidden frames at 12 source frames (not just an artifact of trying 1-pass first) --
  the brief's literal -lag-in-frames 8 does not work with this ffmpeg/libvpx version
  regardless of pass count; lag=16 is the minimum that was tested to work. Full
  bisection table (1-pass lag in {8,10,12,16}, 2-pass lag in {8,16}) in RECIPE.md.
  Expected+observed: coded frame 1 is a genuine hidden altref (show_frame=0,
  refresh_frame_flags=0x04 i.e. refreshes the ALTREF slot only), BUNDLED into a VP9
  superframe together with coded frame 2 (the following shown frame) inside IVF packet
  1 -- VP9-specific: unlike VP8 (Wave 2), where a hidden altref always gets its own
  separate IVF packet, VP9 encoders commonly pack a hidden ARF + the next shown frame
  into ONE superframe/IVF packet (12 IVF packets carry 13 coded frames here).
  sign_bias_alternate_frame (=ref_frame_sign_bias[2]) is 1 on frames 2-11, confirming
  the altref is bitstream-marked as a genuine forward-biased reference, not just
  refreshed-and-ignored. GOLDEN (slot 1) is never refreshed after the keyframe, so it
  stays a 3rd, distinct (older) reference throughout -- three genuinely different
  reference pictures are available for prediction at any point past frame 2 (LAST=most
  recent, ALTREF=filtered/future-biased, GOLDEN=original keyframe), the frame-level
  precondition for compound (two-reference) prediction to be RD-favorable.
  NOTE: no coded frame in this stream uses show_existing_frame (the OTHER libvpx
  mechanism for an ARF-driven 'repeat this reference as output' -- see RECIPE.md
  'known gap' section: a bounded probe at 20 and 30 source frames, and with
  near-static content, never produced one either; V4 should not assume this fixture
  set exercises that path).
  Actual per-block use of two-reference COMPOUND_REFERENCE mode is coded in the
  compressed header (frame_reference_mode(), spec 6.3) which requires arithmetic
  decoding and is out of this static parser's scope -- same scope boundary as Wave 2's
  splitmv per-MB partition-type claim (see split_ivf.py's docstring).
